options.metric: Police-reported crash records per 1,000 elapsed clock-hours in each time period and year
options.denominator: Elapsed clock-hours per period for each complete calendar year (10 hours/day at night, 14 hours/day by day)
options.grouping: Calendar year (2013-2025) and time period: night 20:00-05:59, day 06:00-19:59, unknown time as its own group
options.reason: This framing compares reported crash frequency while accounting for the different numbers of hours in the defined night and day periods.
options.answer: The data answer this only partly: the clock-hour crash rate was higher by day in all 13 years, with 2025 rates of 11,721 day versus 7,028 night crashes per 1,000 clock-hours.
options.interpretation: The data answer this only partly: the chart covers all police-reported crashes in full date-extent years 2013-2025 and divides records by elapsed clock-hours, defining night as 20:00-05:59 (10 hours/day), day as 06:00-19:59 (14 hours/day), and unknown times as a separate 24-hours/day group. The day rate exceeds the night rate in every one of the 13 years; in 2025 the values are 11,721 and 7,028 per 1,000 clock-hours, respectively, making this a defensible way to compare reported crash frequency across periods of unequal duration, but not traveler risk because trip and distance exposure are unavailable. Annual dated crash rows decrease from 203,742 in 2013 to 85,546 in 2025, so the amount of crash reporting behind the yearly rates changes and these rates still do not account for changes in road use. Date extents show 2012 (July-December) and 2026 (January-June 11) are partial and excluded; there are no missing, placeholder, or invalid times, 23,787 midnight times are retained in night though possible default coding cannot be checked, and the unknown-time group has no rows.

options.metric: Percentage of eligible crash records involving at least one reported injury or death
options.denominator: Crash records in each year and time period with nonmissing number_of_persons_injured and number_of_persons_killed
options.grouping: Calendar year (2013-2025) and time period: night 20:00-05:59, day 06:00-19:59, unknown time as its own group; event means injured persons > 0 or killed persons > 0
options.reason: A crash-level injury-or-death share directly compares how often a recorded crash has a reported human harm outcome, rather than just counting crashes.
options.answer: The data answer this only partly: the injury-or-death share was higher at night in 9 of 13 years, while in 2025 it was 42.46% at night and 44.29% by day.
options.interpretation: The data answer this only partly: the chart shows, for 2013-2025, the percentage of crash records with both outcome counts reported where number_of_persons_injured > 0 or number_of_persons_killed > 0, comparing night (20:00-05:59) with day (06:00-19:59) and retaining unknown time as a separate group. Night's injury-or-death share is higher in 9 of 13 years, while day is higher in 2022-2025; in 2025 the respective shares are 42.46% and 44.29%, a defensible measure of harm conditional on a reported crash but not risk per trip or mile. Eligible records fall from 203,742 in 2013 to 85,543 in 2025, so annual percentages are based on differently sized crash populations and the dataset has no road-user exposure denominator. The date-extent check excludes partial 2012 and 2026; of 2,132,218 dated rows in complete years, injury counts are missing in 18 and death counts in 36 (possibly overlapping), which are excluded when either is missing, while 23,787 exact-midnight times are kept in night despite uncertain possible default coding and no missing/invalid time values.

options.metric: Mean reported persons injured per eligible crash record
options.denominator: Crash records in each year and time period with nonmissing number_of_persons_injured
options.grouping: Calendar year (2013-2025) and time period: night 20:00-05:59, day 06:00-19:59, unknown time as its own group
options.reason: The mean injury count captures the reported number of people hurt per crash, adding a crash-severity lens to the frequency and injury-incidence framings.
options.answer: The data answer this only partly: night crashes averaged more reported injured people per crash in all 13 years; in 2025 the averages were 0.595 at night and 0.574 by day.
options.interpretation: The data answer this only partly: the chart reports total number_of_persons_injured divided by crash records with that count present in each full date-extent year from 2013-2025, comparing night (20:00-05:59) with day (06:00-19:59), and putting unknown times in their own group. Night averages more reported injured persons per crash in all 13 years, including 0.595 at night versus 0.574 by day in 2025; this is a defensible crash-severity comparison, but it does not indicate risk per traveler or distance traveled. Eligible crash records fall from 203,742 in 2013 to 85,546 in 2025, so the yearly means are based on different-sized crash groups and cannot adjust for changes in road use. The date-extent check excludes partial 2012 and 2026; 18 of 2,132,218 dated rows in complete years lack an injury count and are excluded, while no crash times are missing/invalid, 23,787 exact-midnight times are retained as night despite uncertain possible default coding, and the unknown-time group has no rows.
